Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:1.hebrew: וסבר ר' שמעון חולין שנשחטו בעזרה דאורייתא - מוזבחת כדפרשינן, דקבעי שחיטה ראויה; דאי רבנן, וטעמא דאסירי משום דמאן דחזי דנשחטו בפנים סבר קדשים נינהו, וחזי דקאכלי להו בחוץ, ואתי למשרי אכילת קדשים בחוץ — מה לי ראויה ומה לי אינה ראויה? הא אתי לאתהנויי מקדשים פסולים:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:1.english: And does Rabbi Shimon hold [that] non-sacred [animals] slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard [are forbidden] by Torah law - [Yes, it is derived] from [the verse] "and you shall slaughter" [Deuteronomy 12:21], as we explained, since he requires a valid slaughter; for if [the prohibition were] rabbinic, and the reason they are forbidden is because one who sees that they were slaughtered inside [the Temple courtyard] thinks they are consecrated offerings, and [then] sees that people eat them outside, and will come to permit eating consecrated offerings outside — what difference is there between a valid [slaughter] and an invalid [slaughter]? Either way, one comes to derive benefit from disqualified consecrated offerings:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:2.english: Yes, and we learned - [To be read] as a straightforward statement [rather than as a question]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:3.hebrew: וכן חיה - אע"ג דכולי עלמא ידעי דלאו קדשים נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:3.english: And likewise, an undomesticated animal - even though everyone knows that [undomesticated animals] are not consecrated [offerings]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:4.hebrew: היינו דגזרינן חיה אטו בהמה - אטו סיפא נקט האי לישנא, דהא ודאי מהיכא דאיתרבי בהמה בקדשים איתרבי חיה, וה"ק: אפילו לא כתיב, בדין הוא דנגזור:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:10:4.english: This is [why] we decree [regarding] an undomesticated animal due to a domesticated animal - It is on account of the latter clause that he used this wording, for certainly from the same [source] that a domesticated animal is included with respect to consecrated [animals], an undomesticated animal is [also] included; and this is what he is saying: even if it were not written [in Scripture], it would be logical that we should decree [it].

Rashi on Chullin 85b:12:1.hebrew: יאניבא - תולעת האוכלת פשתן. טיינ"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:12:1.english: Yaniva - A worm that eats flax, [called] teigne [moth] in Old French:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:12:2.english: Over the tub of water - the steeping water where the flax is:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:12:3.hebrew: דמורח דמא - יריח התולעת ויברח, ששונא הוא לדם עוף:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:12:3.english: So that it smells the blood - The worm will smell [it] and flee, for it hates the blood of a bird:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:13:1.english: And how could he do this - that he does not cover it [the blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:13:2.english: And needs the blood - such as this [case]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:13:3.english: [He is] obligated to cover [the blood] - and he may not use it for his needs:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:13:4.english: How should he act - [so that] he will be exempt from covering [the blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:13:6.english: Tears [it] loose - [He] tears loose the simanim [the windpipe and gullet]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:14:1.hebrew: צא טרוף - עשהו תחלה טרפה, ואח"כ שחוט, דתיהוי שחיטה שאינה ראויה:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:14:1.english: Go out [and] render [it] a tereifa - Make it a tereifa first, and afterward slaughter [it], so that it will be an improper slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:14:2.hebrew: צא טרוף א"ל - רבי לר"ח:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:14:2.english: Go out, render [it] a tereifa, he said to him - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi said this] to Rabbi Chiyya:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:16:1.english: This is its slaughter - and it requires covering [of the blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:16:2.hebrew: כאשר צויתיך - מכלל שנצטוה בעל פה הלכות שחיטה, שהרי בתורה לא מצינו שצוהו:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:16:2.english: As I have commanded you - [This teaches] by implication that he was commanded orally [regarding] the laws of slaughter, for in the Torah we do not find that He commanded him:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:1:1.hebrew: לא לכל אמר רבי מאיר - לא לכל הדברים אמר רבי מאיר שמה שחיטה, כדמפרש דמודי ר"מ שאינה מתירתה באכילה, ולקמן פריך: פשיטא:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:1:1.english: Not with regard to all did Rabbi Meir say - Not for all matters did Rabbi Meir say [that] it is considered slaughter, as [the Gemara] explains, that Rabbi Meir concedes that it does not render [the animal] permitted for consumption; and later [the Gemara] asks: [Is this not] obvious?

Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:1.hebrew: בן ט' חי - דלאו ירך אמו הוא כולי האי, ולענין שחיטה משתרי בשחיטת האם:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:1.english: A living nine[-month-old fetus] - For it is not [considered] the limb of its mother to that extent [as to become a tereifa along with her], yet with respect to slaughter, it is permitted through the slaughter of the mother:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:2.hebrew: סד"א - האי נמי נשתרי בשחיטת הטרפה:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:2.english: It might enter your mind to say - [that] this [fetus] too should be permitted through the slaughter of the tereifa:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - דאינה מתירתה, ובעי למשחטיה, ושחיטת עצמו מתירתו, כדקי"ל (לעיל חולין דף עד.), דארבעה סימנין אכשר ביה רחמנא בבן תשעה חי:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:3:3.english: [It] teaches us - that it [the mother's slaughter] does not permit it, and one must slaughter it, and its own slaughter permits it, as is established for us (above, Chullin 74a), that the Merciful One declared four simanin [the two of the mother or the two of the fetus] valid in [the case of] a living nine-month-old [fetus]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:4:1.hebrew: והא אמר ר"מ - בפרק בהמה המקשה (לעיל חולין דף עד.):
Rashi on Chullin 85b:4:1.english: But doesn’t Rabbi Meir say - [This is] in the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMaksheh (above, Chullin 74a):

Rashi on Chullin 85b:4:2.hebrew: בן פקועה - אפילו היא כשרה, טעון שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:4:2.english: Ben pekua [a fetus found in a slaughtered animal] - Even if she [its mother] is kosher, [the fetus] requires slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:5:1.hebrew: לא צריכא - הא דר' אבא, אלא משום דרבי סבר לה כר' מאיר באותו ואת בנו, כדאמר לעיל:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:5:1.english: [It] is not necessary - this [statement] of Rabbi Abba, [rather it is only needed] because Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir regarding [the prohibition of slaughtering] an animal and its offspring [on the same day], as stated above:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:5:2.hebrew: וסבר לה כרבנן - בבן פקועה, דלא שמעינן ליה דפליג. מהו דתימא: כיון דבן ט' חדשים הוא, ושחיטת עצמו מתירתו אפילו לרבי שמעון — כדקי"ל בפרק בהמה המקשה (שם): ארבעה סימנין אכשר ביה רחמנא — הילכך לאו ירך אמו הוא לאיתסורי משום טרפות דידה, ואימא לרבי, דסבר ליה כרבי מאיר, תהני ליה שחיטת אמו ולא ליבעי למשחטיה, דהא שחוטה היא — קמ"ל:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:5:2.english: And he holds in accordance with the Rabbis - regarding a ben pekua [a living fetus found in a slaughtered mother], for we have not heard him disagree [with them]. What might you have said? Since it is nine [months] old and its own slaughter permits it even according to Rabbi Shimon — as we hold in Chapter Beheimah HaMaksheh (there): "The Merciful One validated four simanim [organs of slaughter] for it" — therefore, it is not [considered] the limb of its mother to become forbidden on account of her tereifah status; and I would say that according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, the slaughter of its mother should be effective for it, and it should not require its own slaughter, since [the mother] is [halakhically] slaughtered — [therefore, Rabbi Abba] teaches us [otherwise]:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:8:1.hebrew: את הטרפה - כגון נחתכו רגליה, טרפות הניכר:
Rashi on Chullin 85b:8:1.english: A tereifa - For example, [where] its legs were severed, a recognizable tereifa:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:8:2.english: And it was found [to be] a tereifa - in [its] internal organs:

Rashi on Chullin 85b:8:3.hebrew: מתיר בהנאה - דשחיטה שאינה ראויה לאו שמה שחיטה, ולא קרינא בהו חולין שנשחטו בעזרה, דזביחה כתיב בהו (דברים יב): "כי ירחק וזבחת" — בריחוק מקום אתה זובח כו' (קדושין דף נז:):
Rashi on Chullin 85b:8:3.english: Permits [deriving] benefit - because a slaughter that is not fit [for consumption] is not considered a slaughter, and we do not apply to them [the prohibition of] non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, for "slaughtering" is written regarding them (Deuteronomy 12): "When [the place] is far... you may slaughter" — in a distant place you may slaughter, etc. (Kiddushin 57b):

Tosafot on Chullin 85b:10:1.hebrew: אין והתנן רבי שמעון אומר כו' - משנה היא בפ' בתרא דתמורה (דף לג:). וממתני' דהכא דפטרינן חולין בעזרה מכסוי לא מייתי, משום דלא נזכר בה ר"ש, אלא "וחכמים פוטרים", ורבי קתני לה. אבל ממתני' דמרובה (ב"ק דף ע.) דפטר רבי שמעון חולין בעזרה מארבעה וחמשה הוה מצי למידק, דאי לא הויא דאורייתא הוה חייב, כדמוכח התם בגמרא (דף עב:); שמא הכא בעי לאוכוחי דאסור בהנאה, וה"ק: מכלל דסבר רבי שמעון דחולין בעזרה אסורים בהנאה דאורייתא? לכך לא מייתי ההיא דמרובה (שם דף ע.), דמהתם לא הוה מצי למידק איסור הנאה אלא איסור אכילה. וא"ת: ומאי קשה ליה, דקא מתמה "וסבר רבי שמעון חולין שנשחטו בעזרה דאורייתא"? וי"ל: משום דאיכא ברייתא בהאיש מקדש (קדושין דף נח.) דקאמר רבי שמעון דהמקדש בחולין שנשחטו בעזרה מקודשת, ומכח ההיא דמייתי מוקי התם בטרפה. ואין נראה, דא"כ הוה ליה לאתויי הכא ההיא ברייתא ולאוקמי בטרפה כדמוקי התם. ונראה לר"ת דקש"ל הך מתניתין גופה דמייתי: דקתני "וכן חיה" — משמע דחיה הוי דרבנן מדקתני "וכן", וא"כ בהמה נמי דרבנן, וקתני "וכן" משום דגזרינן חיה אטו בהמה; דאי מדאורייתא, חיה נמי דאורייתא, ומאי "וכן"? ומשני "אין והתנן", כלומר ומטונך, דמההיא גופה יש לדקדק שהיא דאורייתא, דאי דרבנן הוי חיה גזירה לגזירה:
Tosafot on Chullin 85b:10:1.english: Yes, and we learned [in a Mishnah]: Rabbi Shimon says, etc. - It is a Mishnah in the last chapter of Temurah (33b). And from the Mishnah here, where we exempt non-sacred [animals slaughtered] in the Temple courtyard from covering [the blood], [Abaye] does not bring [a proof], because Rabbi Shimon is not mentioned in it — rather, [it says] "and the Sages exempt," and Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] teaches it. However, from the Mishnah in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 70a), where Rabbi Shimon exempts [one who steals and slaughters] non-sacred [animals] in the Temple courtyard from [paying] fourfold and fivefold [restitution], he could have inferred [it], for if it were not by Torah law, he would be liable, as is proven there in the Gemara (72b). Perhaps here he wants to prove that it is forbidden for benefit, and this is what [Rav Pappa] is saying: Does it follow that Rabbi Shimon holds that non-sacred [animals slaughtered] in the Temple courtyard are forbidden for benefit by Torah law? Therefore, he does not bring that [Mishnah] in Merubeh (ibid., 70a), because from there one could not infer a prohibition of benefit, only a prohibition of eating. And if you ask: What is [Rav Pappa's] difficulty, that he asks in astonishment, "And does Rabbi Shimon hold that non-sacred [animals] that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard are [forbidden] by Torah law?" One can answer: Because there is a Baraita in [the chapter] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 58a), where Rabbi Shimon says that one who betroths [a woman] with non-sacred [animals] that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, she is betrothed; and on account of that [Mishnah] which [Abaye] brings, [the Gemara] establishes [the Baraita] there as referring to a *tereifah* [an animal with a fatal defect]. But [this] does not seem [correct], for if so, [Abaye] should have brought that Baraita here and established it as referring to a *tereifah*, as [the Gemara] establishes it there. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that this very Mishnah which [Abaye] brings was difficult to [Rav Pappa]: for since it teaches, "And likewise a wild beast," it implies that [the prohibition of] a wild beast is rabbinic, because it teaches "and likewise"; and if so, [a domesticated] animal is also rabbinic, and it teaches "and likewise" because we decree [against] a wild beast on account of a domesticated animal — for if [a domesticated animal were forbidden] by Torah law, a wild beast would also be [forbidden] by Torah law, so what [would be the meaning of] "and likewise"? And [Abaye] answers: "Yes, and we learned..." — that is to say, from your own argument [the opposite is proven], for from that very [Mishnah] itself one must infer that it is by Torah law, since if it were rabbinic, [prohibiting] a wild beast would be a decree upon a decree:

Tosafot on Chullin 85b:10:2.hebrew: היינו דגזרינן חיה אטו בהמה - בהאיש מקדש (שם דף נח.) מייתי נמי מהך מתניתין דסבר ר"ש דחולין בעזרה דאורייתא, ואין מאריך שם כמו כאן. ופירש בקונט' דדייק מדהויא בשריפה, דאי דרבנן לא היה טעון שריפה. ואי אפשר לומר כן, דבהדיא מדקדק כאן מכח חיה. וא"ת: דהכא משמע דאפילו הויא דאורייתא, הויא חיה דרבנן, והתם מייתי קרא לאסור בהמה, חיה ועוף? וי"ל דרבי שמעון פליג אההיא ברייתא. ועי"ל דלא פליגי, ונפרש כאן כפירוש הקונטרס דהתם, ואשריפה קאי הכא; דאי אמרת בשלמא דאורייתא בין בהמה ובין חיה ועוף, היינו דגזרינן הכא בחיה שריפה אטו בהמה — אע"ג דבהמה גופה לא הויא בשריפה אלא גזירה אטו קדשים שיצאו לחוץ שהם בשריפה, ובחיה ליכא למטעי אטו קדשים — ולא חשיבא גזירה לגזירה, כיון דאסירא מיהא דאורייתא והויא כולה חדא גזירה; אבל אי דרבנן, אמאי חיה בשריפה:
Tosafot on Chullin 85b:10:2.english: This is why we decree [regarding] an undomesticated animal on account of a domesticated animal - In [the chapter entitled] HaIsh Mekadesh (ibid., 58a), [the Gemara] also brings [a proof] from this Mishnah that Rabbi Shimon holds that [the prohibition of] non-sacred [animals slaughtered] in the Temple courtyard is by Torah law, and it does not elaborate there as [it does] here. And Rashi explained [there] that [the Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that it is [subject] to burning, for if it were rabbinic, it would not require burning. But it is impossible to say so, for here [the Gemara] explicitly infers [it] from the case of an undomesticated animal. And if you ask: Here it is implied that even if it is by Torah law, [the prohibition of] an undomesticated animal is rabbinic, whereas there [in Kiddushin] it brings a verse to prohibit a domesticated animal, an undomesticated animal, and a bird? One can answer that Rabbi Shimon disagrees with that Baraita. And one can also answer that they do not disagree, and we can explain here according to Rashi's explanation there, and here [the Gemara] refers to burning: for granted, if you say [that the prohibition is] by Torah law both [for] a domesticated animal and [for] an undomesticated animal and a bird, this is why we decree burning here in [the case of] an undomesticated animal on account of a domesticated animal — even though a domesticated animal itself is only [subject] to burning as a decree on account of consecrated animals that went outside [the Temple courtyard], which are [subject] to burning, and regarding an undomesticated animal there is no [concern] to err [and confuse it] with consecrated animals — and it is not considered a decree upon a decree, since [an undomesticated animal] is in any case prohibited by Torah law, and it is all [considered] one decree; but if it is rabbinic, why is an undomesticated animal [subject] to burning:

Tosafot on Chullin 85b:3:1.hebrew: אימא תהני ליה שחיטת אמו - דוקא נקט בן ט' חי, אבל מת או בן ח', פשיטא דהוי ירך אמו שהיא טרפה. ואע"ג דאמר באלו טרפות (לעיל חולין דף נח.) דולד טרפה לא הוי ירך אמו, היינו לפי שהוא חי ואין חיותו תלוי באמו. וא"ת: והיכי ס"ד דמשום דרבי סבר לה כר"מ באותו ואת בנו דתיהני ליה שחיטת אמו, הא בכסוי הדם סבר לה כרבי שמעון? וי"ל: דבכל מילי סבר לה כר"מ, דאשכחנא במרובה (ב"ק דף ע.) דסתם לן כר' מאיר בתשלומי ארבעה וחמשה:
Tosafot on Chullin 85b:3:1.english: Say that the slaughter of its mother is effective for it - [The Gemara] specifically stated a living nine-month-old [fetus]; however, [if it is] dead or an eight-month-old [fetus], it is obvious that it is [considered] a limb of its mother, which is a tereifa. And even though [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Tereifot (above, Chullin 58a) that the offspring of a tereifa is not [considered] a limb of its mother, that is [only] because it is alive and its life does not depend on its mother. And if you will ask: How could it enter [one's] mind that because Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds like Rabbi Meir regarding [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring," the slaughter of its mother should be effective for it — behold, regarding covering the blood, [Rabbi] holds like Rabbi Shimon? And one can answer: In all matters [Rabbi] holds like Rabbi Meir, as we find in [the chapter entitled] Merubbah (Bava Kamma 70a) that he taught an anonymous [Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Meir regarding the fourfold and fivefold payment:

Tosafot on Chullin 85b:7:1.hebrew: פשיטא דאמר רב יהודה וכי ימות מן הבהמה כו' - והא דלא מייתי מתניתין דבהמה המקשה (לעיל חולין דף עב:) "לא אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה כו'", משום דהוה מצי למיפרך: בן ח' חי יוכיח:
Tosafot on Chullin 85b:7:1.english: Isn't it obvious? As Rav Yehuda said, "And if there dies of the animals," etc. - And as for why [the Gemara] does not bring the Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Beheimah HaMaksheh (above, Chullin 72b), "No, if the slaughter of a tereifa rendered it pure, etc." — [it is] because one could have objected: A live eight-[month fetus] will prove [otherwise]:

Tosafot on Chullin 85b:9:1.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא הואיל וא"ר שמעון מותר בהנאה - לא מצי למינקט שוחט טרפה והיא אותו ואת בנו, וסד"א דכיון דפטור הוא, לאו שחיטה היא כלל ולא מיטהרה מידי נבלה, דאיכא למימר דלענין שוחט הוא דלא הויא שחיטה, אבל לענין גופה הויא שחיטה; לכך מייתי ראיה, דאף לענין גופה, שתחשב חולין בעזרה לאסור בהנאה, לא הויא שחיטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 85b:9:1.english: It might enter your mind to say: Since Rabbi Shimon says it is permitted to derive benefit - [The Gemara] could not have cited [the case of] one who slaughters a tereifa that is [subject to the prohibition of] "it and its young," and [argued that] it might enter your mind to say that since he is exempt, it is not a slaughter at all and does not purify [the animal] from [the status of] a carcass — for one could say that it is [only] with respect to the slaughterer that it is not a slaughter, whereas with respect to [the animal] itself, it is a slaughter. Therefore, [the Gemara] brings a proof that even with respect to [the animal] itself, so as to be considered non-sacred [meat slaughtered] in the Temple courtyard to be forbidden for benefit, it is not a slaughter:
